meaning: Travelling from one point to the next along fairly straight legs with gentle turns at waypoints.
Steady flight on a straight leg at a constant speed and height.
Fixed-wing drone flying to its next programmed point.
Boat moving between patrol points, steady speed, moderate turns.
Flying low and fast along a leg, with small height changes.
Short straight, level run after a hard manoeuvre to regain speed.
Airliner waiting in a race-track oval (straight leg, 180 deg turn, straight leg, 180 deg turn).
Flying a full circle around a point at constant speed.
Oval pattern: two straight legs joined by two half-circles.
Fighter combat-air-patrol: a long race-track at height and moderate speed.
Drone circling slowly over an area.
Multirotor circling a point of interest at small radius.
Helicopter circling an area while searching.
Boat or skiff going round in a circle (for example around a buoy or net).
Staying in one place in the air with tiny drift (rotorcraft, multirotor).
Helicopter holding a very low hover just before touch-down.
Slowing down to a stop, usually just before a hover.
Helicopter sliding a short distance at low speed close to the ground, then stopping.
Helicopter moving to a new observation spot, then stopping.
Multirotor flying to a point, stopping, hovering, then moving again.
Vessel running, then nearly stopping, then moving again.
Ship cutting speed for a while, then returning to normal speed.
Slow trawling with frequent small course changes.
Almost no propulsion: moving with the current, small heading changes.
Almost stationary, swinging slightly around the anchor.
Gaining height at a steady climb rate.
Losing height at a steady descent rate.
Descending and slowing for landing.
Last straight, low, slow stretch before landing.
Multirotor going straight up or down.
Helicopter sinking straight down to land.
Fighter trading speed for height in a steep climb.
Fighter descending steeply, gaining speed.
Fighter climbing from low level to a higher altitude.
Fighter coming back down to low level.
Powered climb after launch up to cruise altitude.
A high-g turn (several g for fighters).
Short sharp direction change.
Turn that leaves a climb or descent cycle.
Airliner turning off its route to avoid weather, then returning.
A planned course change in the middle of a long flight.
Alternating left/right course changes, regular or evasive.
A short burst of high speed.
Fighter flying fast and straight between turns.
A fast burst, then slowing again.
Multirotor flying at its top speed for a short distance.
The moment a disguised target drops the disguise and accelerates.
Straight flight while speeding up or slowing down.
Back-and-forth lawnmower pattern to cover an area.
Rocket motor burning: very high acceleration.
Lower thrust that roughly holds or slowly changes speed.
No thrust: speed decays because of drag.
Low flight with a gently rolling height profile.
Behaving like an airliner: steady speed and height, gentle turns.
Behaving like a helicopter: slow, low, loitering.
Behaving like a boat: moderate steady speed.
Behaving like a ship: slow, steady, very wide turns.
Behaving like a skiff: small, twitchy, frequent turns.
